cells.B11: Sound-Alikes: drug names that are commonly confused on a call or in handwriting.

cells.B12: Medicare 2027 Basics: Part D deductible and cap, negotiated price drugs, GLP-1 Bridge, what Part D excludes, and C-SNP basics for plan reviews.

cells.B13: Life UW Guide: drug groups with what they may signal to underwriters, general attention level, and questions to ask the client. Last column is for your carrier specific notes.

cells.B17: 1. Enter the generic name when you can. Carriers and underwriting systems generally recognize generic names most reliably.

cells.B18: 2. A drug alone does not equal a diagnosis. Many drugs treat several conditions (gabapentin, propranolol, trazodone, Humira, metformin). Always ask what the medication is for.

cells.B19: 3. Check the Notes column and the Sound-Alikes tab before entering anything that looks close to another name.

cells.B20: 4. If spelling is uncertain, ask the client to read the bottle label or pharmacy printout, including strength and how often it is taken.

cells.B21: 5. Combination products are listed with a hyphen between ingredients. Enter every ingredient if the system asks for them separately.

cells.B22: 6. For Medicare reviews, check the Medicare Part D Notes column first. Some drugs are billed under Part B, excluded by law, or on a specialty tier, and 2027 brings new cost limits.

cells.B23: 7. For life applications, use the Life UW Guide to know which follow up questions to ask before submitting.

cells.C47: Excluded when used for erectile dysfunction
cells.D47: Cialis (tadalafil) is covered for BPH. Sildenafil and tadalafil are covered for pulmonary hypertension.

cells.D48: Proscar (5 mg) for BPH is covered, Propecia (1 mg) for hair loss is not.

cells.B49: Zyrtec, Claritin, Allegra, Benadryl, Tylenol, Aleve, Imodium, Miralax, aspirin
cells.C49: Generally not covered by Part D
cells.D49: Some Medicare Advantage plans include an OTC allowance. Ask what the client is actually paying for today.

cells.C50: Covered by Part D beginning in 2025 (previously excluded)
cells.D50: Some older client formulary notes may be out of date. Check the 2027 formulary.

cells.B51: Infusions, clinic administered injections, Botox, Prolia, Keytruda
cells.C51: Often Part B when given in a provider setting

cells.C52: Part B when used with a nebulizer machine
cells.D52: Hand held inhalers (ProAir, Spiriva, Trelegy) are Part D.

cells.C53: Part B if Medicare paid for the transplant, otherwise Part D

cells.A57: CMS recognizes 15 chronic conditions for C-SNP eligibility: chronic alcohol and other drug dependence, autoimmune disorders, cancer, cardiovascular disorders, chronic heart failure, dementia, diabetes mellitus, end stage liver disease, end stage renal disease requiring dialysis, severe hematologic disorders, HIV/AIDS, chronic lung disorders, chronic and disabling mental health conditions, neurologic disorders, and stroke. A medication hints at a possible fit, but the plan requires a verified diagnosis. High blood pressure and high cholesterol alone do not qualify. Each C-SNP targets specific conditions, so check the plan's summary of benefits. The Drug Reference tab shows a possible C-SNP link for each drug.

cells.A61: CMS Medicare Drug Price Negotiation Program: first 10 drugs effective 2026, next 15 drugs effective January 1, 2027 (cms.gov).

cells.A2: General industry tendencies only, not any carrier's rules. Attention level reflects how closely underwriters tend to look at the condition a drug points to: Low (usually routine if stable), Moderate (details and control matter a lot), High (expect records, ratings or declines), Varies (depends on why it is prescribed). Age, dose, duration, control, and combined conditions change every outcome. Most carriers also check prescription history databases, so list every medication accurately. Use the last column to record what your approved carriers actually do.

cells.E5: Date started, latest cholesterol numbers, any heart attack, stent or stroke history.

cells.C6: High blood pressure. Beta blockers are also used for rhythm problems, anxiety and migraine
cells.E6: Number of BP medications, recent readings, date diagnosed, any heart, kidney or stroke history, and why a beta blocker was prescribed.

cells.B7: Combinations of the drugs above plus spironolactone or clonidine
cells.C7: Hard to control blood pressure, possible kidney or heart disease
cells.E7: Recent readings, kidney function, any hospital visits, other heart conditions.

cells.E10: How often the rescue inhaler is used, ER visits, steroid courses in the last year, tobacco use.

cells.C11: Depression, anxiety, nerve pain, smoking cessation

cells.E12: How often taken, dose, how long, prescriber, alcohol use, other sedating medications.

cells.E14: Age at diagnosis, how long taken, any misuse or substance history.

cells.C16: Bipolar disorder. Lamictal and Depakote are also used for epilepsy and migraine
cells.E16: Why prescribed, hospitalizations, years stable, medication changes.

cells.B17: Antabuse, Vivitrol, naltrexone, Campral, Suboxone, Subutex, methadone
cells.C17: Alcohol or opioid use disorder, possibly in recovery
cells.E17: Date of last use, treatment history, time in recovery, DUI history, relapses.

cells.B18: Chantix, Zyban, nicotine patches or gum
cells.E18: Answer the tobacco question accurately, date of last use. Many carriers test for nicotine.

cells.C19: Chronic pain, recent surgery or injury
cells.E19: Reason, daily dose, how long, prescriber, any substance history. Long term high doses draw more scrutiny.

cells.C20: Nerve pain, seizures, restless legs, fibromyalgia, anxiety

cells.E21: Reason, how long, any underlying disease.

cells.C22: Type 2 diabetes. Metformin is also used for prediabetes and PCOS
cells.E22: Date diagnosed, age, latest A1C, any nerve, kidney, eye or heart complications, height and weight.

cells.E23: Which reason, starting and current weight, A1C if diabetic.

cells.C24: Type 1 diabetes or insulin treated type 2
cells.E24: Type 1 or type 2, age at diagnosis, latest A1C, complications, ER visits for low or high blood sugar.

cells.C25: Atrial fibrillation, blood clots, mechanical valve, stroke prevention
cells.E25: Reason, date of last clot or stroke, other heart conditions, any bleeding events.

cells.C26: Atrial fibrillation or more serious rhythm problems
cells.E26: Type of rhythm problem, date diagnosed, any ablation, pacemaker or defibrillator, ejection fraction.

cells.B27: Entresto, nitroglycerin, Imdur, Ranexa, Lasix with other heart drugs
cells.E27: Ejection fraction, date of last echo, stents or bypass dates, hospitalizations, symptoms.

cells.E28: Procedure date, number of stents, ejection fraction, stress test results.

cells.B29: Spiriva, Trelegy, Breo, Anoro, Daliresp, home oxygen
cells.E29: Smoking status, breathing test results, oxygen use, hospitalizations, steroid courses.

cells.E30: Severity, ER visits, hospitalizations, oral steroid use, tobacco.

cells.C31: Autoimmune disease, COPD, adrenal or other conditions

cells.B32: Humira, Enbrel, Stelara, Cosentyx, Otezla, Rinvoq
cells.C32: Rheumatoid arthritis, psoriasis, Crohn's disease, colitis, ankylosing spondylitis
cells.E32: Diagnosis, severity, date diagnosed, hospitalizations, infections, other medications.

cells.C33: Rheumatoid arthritis, lupus, psoriasis. Methotrexate is also a cancer drug
cells.E33: Why prescribed, dose, liver tests, any other immune medications.

cells.E35: Seizure type, date of last seizure, driving status, medication changes.

cells.E36: Frequency, any neurological testing, other neurological symptoms.

cells.C37: Parkinson's, MS, ALS, Huntington's. Mirapex and Requip are also used for restless legs
cells.E37: Diagnosis, date, stage, mobility, work status. Often declined or heavily rated.

cells.E39: Date diagnosed, CD4 count, viral load, adherence, other conditions. Carrier approach varies widely.

cells.E40: Confirm it is for prevention and HIV negative status. Carriers differ in how they treat and ask about PrEP. Answer every question accurately.

cells.E41: Treatment dates, whether cured, liver tests, cirrhosis.

cells.B42: tamoxifen, anastrozole, letrozole, Xtandi, Zytiga, Gleevec, Revlimid
cells.C42: Cancer history or active treatment. Some are used for prevention or other conditions
cells.E42: Cancer type, stage, diagnosis date, treatment end date, remission status.

cells.E43: Organ, transplant date, complications. Often declined.

cells.E44: Stage, dialysis status, cause, latest kidney tests.

cells.B45: Opsumit, Adempas, Uptravi, Tracleer. Revatio and Adcirca are also sold as sildenafil and tadalafil
cells.C45: Pulmonary arterial hypertension. Sildenafil and tadalafil are also used for erectile dysfunction
cells.E45: Which brand and dose, why prescribed. Often declined for true PAH.

cells.E46: Diagnosis, lung function, hospitalizations. Often declined.

cells.E47: Reason, how long, any prostate or breast history.

cells.E48: PSA history for BPH. For erectile dysfunction, ask about heart and circulation history.

cells.E49: Fractures, falls, long term steroid use.

cells.E50: Kidney function, how often flares occur.

cells.E51: Height and weight, how long taken, other weight related conditions.

cells.E52: Reason. Ask why if a client takes one every day long term.

cells.E54: Ask why it was prescribed, such as along with an opioid prescription.

cells.A2: Purpose: build the agency's own record of how each approved carrier handles specific drugs and conditions, so producers can shop with confidence. How to use: add one row per carrier, product and drug or condition. Pick Product Line and Decision from the dropdowns. Record the exact details (rating, wait period, lookback) and the source (guide name and date, or rep name and date). Delete the example row once your own entries are in. Review entries at least yearly since carrier guides change.
